gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the quiet-mode figures behind its ranking come from three different test setups that cannot be lined up. Only Bambu gives a distance (P2S: under 50 dB in Silent Mode at 1 m). Elegoo's 45 dB for the Centauri Carbon 2 is a lab reading in Silent Mode with the auxiliary part-cooling fan switched off, at no stated distance. Anycubic's 44 dB for the Kobra S1 has no stated distance or speed. Bambu owners report that Silent Mode runs at 50% speed. A 1 m vs 0.5 m difference alone is worth about 6 dB, more than the 44-vs-50 dB gap the ranking rests on.
standout_why: Compared against the cited pages Product Bible (quietest-3d-printers), 3D Printer World (best-enclosed-3d-printer) and StarterBench (P1S vs P2S), plus the top results Additive Realm (66-machine ranking). Product Bible already says every figure is the maker's own and lists Elegoo's aux-fan-off condition and Bambu's 1 m distance (H2S). 3D Printer World gives the P2S 1 m distance and the CC2 aux-fan-off note. Additive Realm shows a Prusa MK4 reading of 55-65 dB at 0.5 m against 45-50 dB at 2 m. None puts the conditions side by side, says that only Bambu's figure has a distance, gives the speed cost of Bambu's Silent Mode, or states that Kobra S1 at 44 dB vs P2S under 50 dB is not a measured 6 dB win. So rivals have parts of it. The half-speed Silent Mode figure comes only from Bambu forum users, not from Bambu, which limits how much it can decide.
decides: It weakens ChatGPT's 'Kobra S1 is quietest' pick, which rests on unlike maker numbers. The only claim with a distance (P2S under 50 dB at 1 m) is not shown to be louder than Kobra S1's ≤44 dB or CC2's 45 dB, because those carry no distance, and Elegoo's has the part fan off. A fair page ranks on independent same-distance measurements, or says it can't. For a shopper it also says that every 'silent' figure costs print speed (Bambu Silent Mode is about half speed by owner reports). QIDI Q2, Plus5 and Max4, which Dealectric lists, publish no dB figure at all, so they can't enter a spec ranking.

findings.label: Distance effect on a dB reading
findings.value: About 6 dB per doubling of distance (free field); Prusa MK4 55-65 dB at 0.5 m vs 45-50 dB at 2 m
findings.source_title: Additive Realm: Quietest 3D Printer: Noise Ranking of 66 Machines
findings.note: The MK4 readings are Additive Realm's. The 6 dB is inverse-square arithmetic, 20·log10(2) = 6.02 dB, an ideal free-field figure (rooms reflect, so the real change is smaller). So a ≤44 dB claim taken at 0.5 m would equal about 38 dB at 1 m, and one taken at 2 m about 50 dB at 1 m. Without a stated distance, 44 vs 50 dB does not rank the two printers.
